title: Client-side lease-backed usage seals to prevent duplicate charge on flaky networks
creator: Riley Patel
description:
Problem: We continue to see customer-reported duplicate billing incidents stemming from at-least-once delivery semantics between client SDKs and the ingest tier (timeouts, retries across mobile/edge networks). Existing server-side dedupe approaches (global nonce registries and ephemeral replay tokens) are effective but contribute latency and a higher storage/coordination cost for high-volume, short-lived requests (embeddings, small text generation calls).

Proposed approach: Introduce a lightweight client-side 'usage seal' protocol where the client obtains a short-lived lease (sealed nonce) from the ingest gateway prior to making a billing-affecting request. The client will attach the usage seal to the request. The gateway guarantees that each seal can be consumed exactly once for billing accounting; on duplicate attempts with the same seal the gateway will return an idempotent success or a specially-coded duplicate-response without recharging. Leases are intentionally small (TTL ~30s) and rotate frequently to limit state footprint. When network conditions are flaky, the client can proactively renew or request a 'continuation seal' tied to a parent lease to allow safe retry without recharging.

Why this is different: Instead of relying solely on server-side long-lived global dedupe stores or client-only heuristics, the lease seal balances coordination cost and correctness by using transient, lease-backed seals that the gateway can track in a bounded in-memory cache and a compact tombstone log. This reduces permanently stored dedupe state and aligns well with our autoscaling dedicated pools because leases are cheap to validate and expire quickly.
acceptance_criteria: Client SDKs (JS, Python, Go) can obtain, attach, and rotate usage seals to requests
Gateway validates a seal and ensures single-charge semantics (duplicate consumes do not increment metered usage)
System supports continuation seals for safe retries within a single logical operation
End-to-end tests demonstrate no double-charge for simulated flaky retry scenarios across 10k requests
Monitoring: new dashboard shows seal issuance rate, duplicate-detection rate, cache hit/miss, and tombstone growth
Reconciliation job detects any unsealed requests and surfaces potential customer-impacting anomalies
updates: 2026-03-02: Spike completed; validated in-memory lease cache with LRU+TTL can keep footprint under 40MB for 50k leases per gateway instance (Sasha).
2026-03-04: Design review with PM and Runtime — agreed to use 30s default TTL and continuation seals instead of unlimited retries to avoid long-lived tombstones (Morgan).
2026-03-06: SDK work started (JS prototype attaches seals to requests). Initial failures observed on multipart upload flows; need to pass seals through upload presign flow (Avery).

2026-03-09: Load test showing gateway validation adds ~0.6ms P50 per request when running local cache hit; miss penalty ~3ms due to tombstone check. Ops accepts perf budget for P99 under current targets.
2026-03-12: Security review requested — sealing protocol validated against replay attacks but KMS integration required for cross-region trust; filed follow-up (ENG-679045).
notes: Implementation plan: 1) Add Lease API endpoint on gateway (issue/GET-> returns sealed token bound to client_id, request_fingerprint). 2) Client SDK: obtain seal, attach header X-Usage-Seal, track local TTL and implement renewal/continuation semantics. 3) Gateway: validate seal in fast path using in-memory cache; on consume mark tombstone with minimal metadata (customer_id, usage_delta) and asynchronously persist compact ledger checkpoint for reconciliation. 4) Reconciliation: extend existing billing sweep to detect mismatches between tombstone ledger and final consumption records. 5) Rollout: staged rollout to 10% of traffic with canary metrics and fallback to legacy dedupe.
risks_and_mitigation: Lease expiry during slow requests -> mitigation: continuation seals allowing single extension with parent link
Clock skew between client and gateway -> mitigation: include server-signed expiry and accept small skew window
Increased gateway state -> mitigation: enforce strict TTL, LRU eviction, and tombstone compaction background job
Compatibility with private deployments (on-prem) -> mitigation: feature flag and documented ops knobs for tombstone persistence policy
